body: Victoria Park, Nuwara EliyaFirst thing to note, although this is common, foreigners (you) get charged 300 rupees to enter. Locals are free. We paid our fee to the lady behind the counter. As I turned around a male guard asked to check my ticket. He’d just seen me buy it but never mind. We saw signs stating no plastic bottles or bags were allowed as they become litter. The place was filthy with litter of all types but mostly plastic bottles. In one of the free flowing water areas there were several old tyres which had clearly been there for ages. It was obvious the bottles were not all from the day before due to the condition or grubbiness of them. We picked some up and gave them to one of the many guards and staff but there was too much for us to manage. No one appeared to be proactively litter picking when our perception was that a person could have been tasked with this. There was clearly ongoing work judging by the piles of garden debris but again our perception, this appeared to an effort to tidy the place up when it had been neglected over time. We noticed some of the plants were covered in graffiti scratched into their leaves. Some people eh! But then we saw what appeared to be locals rather than foreigners doing exactly that. Despite the wealth of staff and uniformed guards this behaviour was unchallenged so we did, loudly.These plants surrounded a water feature which was not in operation. There was a wooden jetty into the feature which looked 20 years past its prime, basically derelict and in need of removal. I know this is not main season so the gardens would not be at their best but the overall impression was of poor and overdue management. Overall we were disappointed and would not recommend this unless you have nothing else to do. So we left and walked up to the nearby lake which was even worse! Again we were asked to buy a ticket, from where we were we could see rubbish floating everywhere. Don’t bother unless you want to see a few horses tethered. Nuwara Eliya is grossly overrated and was a shame to waste two booked nights there.
title: Poorly managed. Not worth the entrance fee.

body: My wife and I visited here during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka. This park as well as being beautiful is also International renowned as a must visit Birding location. Several of the beds were already being replanted. Around the perimeter of the park there is a very smelly river, this was a magnet for many of the birds including some really sought after species - Kashmir Flycatcher, Pied Thrush, Forest Wagtail, Dusky Warbler and Sri Lanka Bush Warbler. We were so impressed we’re planning a second visit during our stay in Nuwara Eliya. Highly Recommended

body: Victoria Park is a public park located in Nuwara Eliya, next to the Nuwara Eliya Post Office.The park was formally named in 1897 to commemorate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.The park was established with the planting of its first tree, an Oak, by a visiting German Princess. The Nanu Oya River runs through the park, creating a number of small lakes. A number of rare bird species can be found in the park. At the far end of the park is a small children's playground and miniature rideable railway.(Wikepedia).If you are a nature lover, then this is an ideal place to relax with your loved ones. The beautiful flowers, the huge trees that gives its green, and the walkways, Now at presented its upgraded with paved roads, and there is an entrance fees, when we were kids we used to cross the park after school, and play around the grasslands. body: I think Victoria Park is a gorgeous place. I’m somewhat surprised at the people who have quibbled over the payment of a fee of, little more than $1.50, after all this is what you would pay in tips for a piece of cake and a coffee in North America. So it’s worth putting the fee into perspective. It’s also worth putting into context the location of the park in Nuwara Eliya. Situated just next to the busy, cacophonous bus depot, it still manages to provide an amazingly tranquil experience. Granted the museum is a bit odd, and the cafe/eating area could do with greater imagination in terms of appeal, but the rest is heavenly. I would advise going at the very start of the day, you get to see the workers carefully tending the park’s flowers, and you hear sounds and see wonderful, characterful bird life. Just listening to the sounds was a tranquil experience. For such a small park, there’s a lot packed it, but it won’t appeal to those who just want to tick a box, to day they have visited the place, or who are too mean to part with a dollar. I was there for 3 hours, just resting and listening but, be aware, around lunchtime, it gets busy as (on the day I was there) crowds of children and tourists seemed to arrive in a short spell.

body: Is it a nice Park?YesIs it worth 200 (for foreigners)?NOOO!Very basic park which one can find in every city.
title: Just any other park

body: One of the famous garden in "Nuwaraeliya". This park is located at "Nuwaraeliya" town. Walking distance from bus stand. It is small compared to "Hakgala" botanical garden. But anyway when you travel to " Nuwaraeliya" city you can stay at this place little time and get relax. Inside this garden you can capture photos with flowers. You may stay in this garden less than one hour. Because inside there is nothing special to see as compared to other parks.This is one of the famous place among local couples of Sri Lanka. Anyway this place is very good for children to play, because of open space. Parking space and washroom facilities available maintaining by municipal counsil.They may charge for parking.If you go long journey and if you are gonna plan to stay at "Nuwaraeliya" city. This is one of the nice place to end up journey and relax some time.
title: "You can have short walk through the park"

body: Seemed a bit steep to pay R300 to get in for what is just an ordinary, park with a few small gardens. However it’s a haven for birdwatching where we saw a pied thrush as well as a number of endemic Sri Lankan birds. Loads of twitchers in the park actually and some very helpful local ones too.
title: Ok park but great for twitchers!

body: We visited here in the early morning looking for birds and it was SO peaceful just strolling around amongst an immaculately kept garden full of amazing trees, shrubs and plants.
title: Stunningly beautiful

body: It’s just the local park, not intended as a tourist destination, but as there is not much to do in Nuwara Eliya, if you have spare time you could go for a pleasant walk there. There is nowhere much to shelter if it is raining though, so better on a nice day. It has a large pond, a rose garden, lots of trees and a fountain.
title: A nice walk, but nothing special for the entrance fee

body: I would not recommend this place for non-Sri Lankans. If you want well kept gardens in Nuwara Eliya you should visit some of the hotel gardens nearby; The Grand, The Hill Club or St Andrews Jetwings. These are all free and much, much better.Victoria gardens is a baffling 300rs for tourists and 10-15rs for locals. Definitely more of a park than ‘gardens.’ I would not visit again.
title: Supremely average tourist trap

body: Pleasant enough place to wander around for an hour or two. Some interesting trees and plants and a good play area for kids. 300 rupees entry for foreigners. Small museum but not much in it. Lots of well dressed school kids who are always interested in talking to you in their rather shy and naive manner.
title: Ok

body: It is definitely not a highlight. Average - unless you want to walk to relax. If you lack time, you will not miss much.
title: A place where local couples meet

body: This park opens at 8am and closes around 7pm. Tickets for locals are Rs. 60/- and a bit expensive for foreigners. This park was known for a lot of birds and bird spotting & photography but when I went last week there were hardly any birds in the morning and evening session. They do have a public car park outside. Toilets inside the park stink so don't think of using it. It's a small park in the Nuwara Eliya town so you might end up spending less than an hour here.
title: Good place to relax with family and kids

body: Lovely large gardens in the centre of Nuwara Eliya provide a welcome place to retreat from the bustling town. The park has a many trees shrubs and flowers and attracts much birdlife.
title: Mrs

body: We had a nice walk around the park but it's really nothing special, especially having been to Kandy Botanical Gardens and walking through the beautiful country side around Nuwara Eliya. We did see a lot of bird watchers so presumably its good for that. Maybe it has more going on at other times of the year....
title: Average park you pay to enter

body: 15 minutes max in this park, not much to see, and you have to pay for the visit... Go to the botanical garden instead!!!
title: Pay for nothing to see

body: We really enjoyed walking around Victoria Park. Very nice trees, well manicured lawn and plants and it's just fun to people watch here. Everyone was having a good time, including three Buddhist monks who were constantly taking selfies of each other. In tis busy, crowded and noisy city, it's a nice refuge from the craziness.
title: Very nice park in the middle of a busy city

body: One of the well known attractions in Nuwara Eliya. Located In the city centre. There are 2 entrances. Very beautiful park with various kind of flowers, lush green lawn, and small paths to every where.. The most popular area is the children play ground.
title: Beautiful park with children play area

body: Really odd to have to pay to walk around a park. Nothing special about it really. It is quiet and has some lovely areas of flowers fairly typical of a park.
title: Typical park

body: The atmosphere and the views were amazing, the trees and the flowers were well engineered and the weather was super pleasant, I would recommend this place for everyone looking for a quiet place and fresh air.
title: Beautiful place

body: Our guest stay looked over the park and we thought we would have a look.Entrance was 500rp if I remember correctly and it wasn’t worth it.The Park wasn’t as nice as it could be and needed a lot of work.To give it credit we were there just after the planting of the annuals so in 3 months it could be a different story.Lots of locals enjoying the gardens and met the gardeners who were very proud of their garden.Needs work to honour the entrance fee.Not Missing much if you walk around it
title: Ho hum.Not Worth the Entrance Fee

body: Victoria Park is very beautiful with thousands of years old trees, many different types of plant species. Where i have hardly seen any ehere else. It is well maintained and designed in such a way. That every one can relax and spend time here. Children were playing in their own areas. Couples were relaxing and enjoying the peaceful environment. Chatting and sitting care free on the green velveteen grass spread all over the garden. Elderly people were walking around with their grand children. Happily chatting and moving in different areas. We spend almost two hours there then also some parts were left to explore, it's big and Must visit in Nuwara Eliya.
title: Big and Old but beautifully designed and kept

body: Good place to walk. Garden is not well maintained and a number of flower beds were found to be barren. However, the older trees were beautiful as were the green lawns.
title: Smaller than Peradenya Botanical Gardens

body: When you need killing some time in Nuwara Eliya, and have checked-out already the various quirky old English style buildings (Post Office, Office of the Police Superintendent, etc.), and when you're tired of the hussle and bussle of the shopping street, this park offers an oasis pf quietness. For a small entrance fee it's nice to have a quiet stroll, and look at old palm trees or check-out some manicured planted area's (for example in the Japanese garden).
title: nice for a stroll, killing time

body: For 300LKR you can enter this park. It has everything a park usually has. And having that said, it is nothing special. There is an area specially made for children where they can play.
title: A park

body: A good variety of plants and flowers, well maintained park, serene atmosphere. Not a very large place though
title: Good place to spend time

body: The beauty of this park catch my attention to see what’s the true meaning of natural nature. I’m very thankful because I’ve been in this beautiful place. Thank you for all the people here in Sri Lanka!
title: Trees 🌲!

body: We arrived & paid for our ticket. After walking around for a few minutes we notice the sheer amount of rubbish witch had be left, mainly in the Rivers which come through the park. As we were leaving the park (main entrance) something caught my eye. It was a small shine, as I went over I noticed there was a collection box with a large swastika on it. At this point I was so disgusted I left straight away!!!
title: Small shine with swastika logos on found in park!

body: This was a nice garden situated in Nuwara Eliya .We had lunch siting here during our visit to Kandy while on our Sri Lanka tour organized by Arooha tours. This place has nice flowers near by stalls and pony rides as well
title: Lovely place and cool

body: Only went in to kill some time. Nothing much to see - took 10 minutes to walk through it. As usual, an entrance fee vigourously enforced - not much in the scheme of things - but annoying anyway.
title: Boring and another foreigners fee to enter

body: Spent a long time here looking at the wonderful trees and a few flowers as not the best season for blooms. Met Tony the head gardener we think very knowledgeable & gave us a few blooms to hold camphor leaves to smell fantastic man
title: Well worth the money

body: Looks like this park may have been grand at some point in the past but not at the moment. Was overgrown and in need of some TLC
title: Needing maintenance

body: The park is not well maintained at all! Its cheap to enter but still not worth the money. Maybe you will find some intressting birds as we saw a lot of photorgraphers but the park is not nice at all.
title: Is this a park???

body: Quite big and stunning park located in the heart of the town. Best for an evening stroll or a picnic.
title: Beautiful Park

body: Nothing that special to see. Looks like in history place has had nice fountains and bonds but now it's bit sad. Water/bonds is full of plastic trash.
title: Not worth the 300 rupias entrance fee

body: The park is quite large and a peaceful enclave away from the bustle of the town, even though it's a very short walk from the bus station. The biggest issue is litter. There is a SLR300 charge for foreigners - it wouldn't take much to employ some litter pickers from this.
title: Could be so much nicer

body: Nice gardens give a break from city life. Big enough to walk and explore. 300 rupees entrance fee for foreign visitors
title: Nice place to lounge in the shade of a tree

body: As usual a small foreign tourist entrance fee but not expensive , Lots of flowers and a Japanese Garden . Really it’s best because it’s very noisy once you exit the park to the shops and bus station.
title: Small entrance fee

body: At the gate after buying entry tickets you are guided towards the museum, big sign Silence, black and white photos the latest 1940.The park no flowers at this time of year, scruffy with big signs saying No Playing in the Park, and Behave with decorum.Enjoy at your peril!
title: One of the worst ever

body: This is a modest sized park with a lot of history. It`s busy, well used ,safe for all. the audience is mainly the young kids plus 25-40`s. No loud music,has a cafe and little areas with attractions that make a stroll worthwhile. You could do it all in no more than 30 minutes
title: A reasonable oasis near the hectic town/bus station

body: Nice to stretch the legs. Have a look at the post office slightly down the road in Swiss? Architecture. I would not go out of my way just for the park but it is nice if you are passing by. through.
title: Not bad... Not bad.

body: Not a great park, it is littered around the water way, what a shame! Nothing is flowering in January, however some of the trees are impressive.
title: Nice trees

body: It is just an ordinary park but a tourist attraction of this area. Good for families but not a park for full day activity. There is a children play area inside as well but on rainy day it is very messy.
title: Average park

body: This is probably a nice park in season, but in January it has little to offer except green lawns populated by pick-nicking groups and--unfortunately--feral dogs.The park was mostly clean, and there are three types of bins set up to encourage recycling. No signs in English on those, so you will have to open them up to gauge what is appropriate. However, there are some signs in English: one of them admonishing us to "Behave Decently." I did my best.It is only Rs. 300 to get in.
title: Out of season in January

body: Lovely park to spend an hour or two.Everything is very well maintained and the flowers are beautiful.I walked around for about an hour, then sat and read a book.Very “British” feel to it.
title: Beautifully maintained park

body: Victoria Park is quite large and beautifully green. Well worth a stroll around, especially the herb garden.
title: A very nice English style park

body: Its only 300 rupees each but nothing was in flower etc so not worth a visit in my view. Other times of year may be better of course.
title: January visit not worth the entry fee

body: This is nice and in the middle of town - but it’s very small and lots of litter which really makes it unpleasant in parts - expensive for what it is
title: Tiny and litter

body: It's an ordinary garden, nothing great about it.We just walked around and we're out in less than an hour.Don't spend money and time on this location.
title: Can be skipped, nothing great

body: The park is dated and lacks safety aspects to ensure children do not hurt themselves. Nothing great to see or write about. We only went because we had spare time whilst waiting for our car.Very mediocre.
title: For young kids

body: Went in Jan and no beautiful flowers and roses visible. Park was clean except for the stream that runs through the park which was smelly and had garbage. Should be way different in the April season. The play area was good for kids, the train was cool and may of the equipment. But the bouncy castle was dirty and the Ferris wheel looked dangerous. The grass was over grown and the ride areas were quite muddy. Entry ticket was cheap and nice place to watch the world pass by.
title: Nothing much in Winter, but Spring is great

body: Having paid the entry fee we were disappointed with the state of the gardens. Maintenance seemed to be lacking in many places and the children's play area didn't offer much more than 10mins worth of distraction for our two. The miniature train is cute, but it didn't entice our kids to wait in line.
title: Not as nice as we had been led to understand

body: Not much to see in January in the gardens. The little stream was full of rubbish and the lawns needed mowing. OK for a quick visit on a nice day.
title: Needs better maintenance

body: The Park is clearly a honeypot for local people as well as visitors. We enjoyed our walks here. The Park is immaculately maintained, or at least those parts in general view. We also followed the stream and walked through woodland and here there is rubbish galore. We were seeking birds and that was successful.
title: Very popular

body: Well maintained, clean, calm. A good break from the more energetic surroundings and a nice path through the city. A small shop in the middle serve tea etc.Entry fee LKR 300.
title: Very sweet spot - a perk in the city

body: Foreigners are charged 300 rupees to visit and that is fine if the park was kept in good condition. In December it all looks a bit 'tatty' - a park gardener was happy to tell us how lovely it looks in April. So for now, just a place to stroll for 20 minutes!
title: Slightly neglected - maybe better in the spring!

body: Definitely a must see in Nuwara Eliya, but please be mindful that this is a very small park. One could finish walking around in 30 minutes or less. We took our time and just enjoy walking inside of the park.
title: A quaint little park

body: This is a lovely open space in the middle of the town. We visited for the birdlife that can be seen there. Early morning is the best time before there is too much disturbance from human visitors. As well as the obvious egrets in the open areas there are different birds all along the stream and vegetation on the opposite side of the park. This is a site for wintering Pied ThrushAt the time of one of our visits see saw two wedding parties having photographs taken.There are small kiosks for buying drinks and snacks.Odd quirk - mens and womens toilets are at opposite sides of the park.
title: Well kept town park and appreciated by birds too

body: If you visit Nuwaraeliya the one place that you should not miss is Victoria Park. It's nicely maintain lot of various kinds of flowers. Good walk around the park refreshing your mind
title: It's nicely maintain

body: One of the oldest Gardens in Sri-Lanka, still well maintained, has the old world charm.Good to relax on a sunny day.
title: A Lovely Garden

body: Nice relaxing park - crazily English except the fact that you have to pay to get in! Well maintained and very clean. Well policed and very safe. Ok children's area which gave our kids some space to run around. Ok for a spare relaxing afternoon if you have one.
title: Ok place for an afternoon

body: Loved the place and the endless array of trees and flowers. Nice place for a stroll with a loved one. Quiet and serene. Be sure to bring a sweater
title: A taste of Little England

body: By chance we bumped into the head gardener who gave us a very good tour. I suspect he does this for a few tourists and we did give him a tip. We left with a much better knowledge of plants in Sri lanka. At 300 LKA to enter its only a couple of UK £ so we did not begrudge that . And compared with the nearby town bustle and fumes its a place of peace and quiet. It was also close to our hotel so a pleasant walk.
title: Try to catch the gardener for a tour

body: Not being used to having to pay to visit a public park I guess one feels a little hard done by when all our parks are free to all. At 300 LKR I guess it is not a lot but the standard then one would expect to be higher. A asmall variety of colour was on display. Apart from the odd tree label none of the flower beds gave any description. Obviously popular to the locals on a Sunday with a children's area also. Really only an average garden good for a stroll.
title: Worth a visit I guess

body: Nice city garden in the middle of city. Have children play area. Good for walk for elders. I feel entry tickets should not be there at morning times for elder tourist who go there for morning walks.
title: City garden

body: We wanted to visit the childrens park. Unfortunately only accessible through the park, meaning that we had to buy a 300 rps ticket. Park is pretty and well kept, but we thought the entrance fee was a bit steep. Toilets are filthy.Childrens park was fun to while away an hour with two under 5's. Attractions have got some sharp edges and are generally quite run down. There is a rather dodgy ferris wheel - we went for a ride but it was spinning at great speed and afterwards this no longer felt like such a good idea.
title: Well kept but bit pricy

body: The Victoria Park is much like a botanical garden with varied trees and flowering plants. It also has sprawling green lawns and a play area for kids. The entry fee is LKR 300 and is open from 7am to 7pm on all days. The park was christened in 1897 to commemorate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.
title: Its expensive but must visit if you like Nature

body: It's just fine, not as good as the Botanical Garden in Kandy but great if you want to walk around and see Srilankan families relaxing.
title: It's just fine, not as good as the Botanical Garden in Kandy

body: dont go on weekends,it was very near to our hotel.enjoyed a quiet long walk here on a mid week day.it was comparetively cheaper than other tourist attracrions for foriegners
title: good quiet walk

body: Head gardener gave us a special tour through "his" park. He was very knowledgeable having studied 2 years in Kandy, owning many books of German botanical gardens and working already 16 years in this park. Many flowers and trees were presented by their German name. Although I have to agree with another feedback that there is waste laying around, the excellent tour outweighed this fact by far!
title: Excellent tour by head gardener

body: When we visited the were school children in groups in the park,reminded the park in kandy we visited 2days before,
title: Lovely Place

body: The park was quite nice with some enjoyable spots, but it was not exceptional so the entrance fee (only for foreign) is not justified. In some places there are some stray dogs that tried to attack people
title: Nice place but you have to pay for the entrance

body: This is a very large park, very well maintened grassland and trees. Together with other neighboring public parks and lake makes this Nuwara Eliza looks like a very nice European or a new world town. A good place to relax or take your kids to ride on a pony.
title: Nice place to relax

body: The pack is really nice (except for requiring to pay entrance fee!) - there's a kids corner, where you can find the unique attraction. Diesel-engine powered faris wheel! You may even see the staff climbing up to the top and hanging on the cart to get it spinning. It's quite surreal to see... :)
title: Dont miss the faris wheel!

body: Not quite sure why you have to pay to walk around a park but there you go - pleasant enough 30 - 45mins unless you have kids maybe longer.
title: Ok for a quick look- see

body: The best part is the children park if you have kids, entrance fees 300 repuee. Recommended for maximum 1 hour
title: OK but not WOW

body: In the middle of the city you'll find this calm park, wide area contains many species of trees and flowers and they have a special corner for the birds
title: Good garden for relaxing

body: Lovely park to wander around or relax in. A small fee for foreign guests of 300 rupees. Worth a visit.
title: Very pretty park

body: Its a good place to be with kids families friends or with your partner. Either you want to relax on the grassy ground and benches or walk in between huge flower beds. Huge botanical variation of flowers and plants. Decorated with water fountains and nice little paths. Recommend for families and this is one of the must see locations in Nuwara Eliya..
title: Relax or Fun

body: We strolled through the park after having been cooped up in our room due to cxld program and rain.A nice park. Not big, not fancy, but clean.For us it was a breath of fresh air (in both meanings) as Nurawa Eliya was such a disappointment for us.
title: Nice place to while away half an hour or so

body: Victoria park is quite nice and well kept - you have to pay to enter but it's a nice activity as Nuwara Eliya offers few things to do. The park is quite big and has a lot of places to sit. There is a play area for children.
title: Something to do

body: The queen victroia park is located by the nuwara eliya city. victroria park is a place to relax and enjoy the natural sight and clean mountain air.this place is famous for bird watching and there are large verities of plants and trees available. victoria park come alive with the flowers specially around march to may, and august and September. we will come victoria park again.
title: "Relax Place"

body: We enjoyed visiting the park. We saw few birds amidst of windy weather. Flowers are blossoming. I could show some tourists Sri Lanka National flower and some endemic birds of Sri Lanka.
title: a place to to relax!

body: Nice and clean park in the middle of the city. Nice to walk with the kids. Funny children play park (try the big wheel).
title: Very nice park to take a walk

body: Lovely, well manicured garden with huge variety of flowers all of which were in bloom in August. Very relaxed environment and pleasant place to take a walk. Seems popular with tourists and locals alike.
title: Very pretty

body: Been this wonderful place just after my wedding as a honeymoon location. It's a superb environment with very fresh air in the central province of Sri Lanka. Highly recommended for couples who wish to spend time leisurely in a clean environment in Sri Lanka. Love this place
title: Superb Honeymoon Location

body: All the foreigners have to pay the entrance fee and it is not worth the entrance fee spent and you can spend driving around the hills for this time.
title: Not worth spending money as entrance fee

body: Victoria park is a fairly typical Victorian style park, only in Sri Lanka. The gardens are not particularly well maintained and there are signs that say you cannot play in the park. With an entry fee that is a little on the hefty side, I felt it was not good value.
title: A victorian park that needs a bit of TLC in the gardening department

body: The park ia beautifully landscaped. There is a rose garden but it wasnt in bloom. The trees and smalls ponds are lovely. There is a good childrens play area as well with all kinds of swings.
title: Beautiful kid friendly park

body: Not a must visit. If you have spare days 8n Nuwara Eliya have a visit in the cold evening rather than morning.
title: Not bad

body: Perhaps the time of the year isn't right as we didn't see many flowers blooming. Small garden for evening walks. Completed it less then an hour.
title: Small garden

body: This is some wonderful green experience. It has Lilly garden very well maintained. You can complete the park within 2 hours very easily by walking.
title: Great place for nature lover

body: Perfect place for a walk if you stay in Nuwara eliya town. Nice atmosphere for a relax time. There are few food spots where you can buy snacks and all fruits. Great place to kids
title: Best place for a walk

body: This is the one of attractive garden in Nuwara Eliya. Nice place to walk and lots or beautiful flowers. If you go to Nuwara Eliya you should reserve your time to visit this beautiful garden.
title: A nice place

body: Finding beautiful gardens with lovely flowers and various areas to just unwind and relax is just wonderful. There's a kiddies area as well (thank goodness).
title: A nice place to unwind

body: We visited one morning and spent a couple of hours wandering about looking at the flowers. The thing which made thus such a brilliant experience was only that the Gardener Tony started chatting to us and basically gave us a free guided tour telling us about each flower. I'm not that into flowers personally but his enthusiasm was so infectious that you couldn't help but enjoy it!
title: Brilliant gardener

body: It is a normal park where you can go for a walk and spend some time.Not a must go place but if you have leisure time then you can go for a walk.
title: A park for walk

body: This is a beautiful park and located in the centre of the city. It was wonderful, walking through the gardens among the colourful flowers and pin trees, and reviving childhood memories.Good to see that security is vigilant and misbehaviour monitored closely, but litterers should be equally closely monitored. Rather amusing to see signs that exhorted couples to 'behave decently' There was some rubbish near the natural stream near the entrance, which rather spoiled the pristine beauty of the park. The rose garden was not as verdant as I remembered, though, which was rather sad, but given the vast expanse that has to be maintained, this was forgivable.I don't agree with people who don't want to pay to enter. This is a poor country and money is needed for maintaining attractions such as these.The fact that it is for the entire family means that couples really should 'behave decently' - the verdant landscapes of Nuwara Eliya give them much more scope for romance.
title: Beautiful and maintained fairly well

body: This is pretty ancient part with lush green grass and variety of flowers. I am sure you gonna like it. The park also have a connectivity to children park with lots of swings options for kids. Park has entrance fees of 300 LKR per person. But a must go place.
title: Very beautiful park and well maintained

body: Park entry is 300 roepies for a foreigner, 40 for a local.For Sri Lanka standards, that is pretty high.So I was very dissapointed to see all the plastic rubbish lying in the park in the ditches, all the grass groing out of the pavement, and some buildings needing a make over 10 years ago already....
title: Not much

body: Before we arrived here we think this park to be nice place to visit. But when we entered the park it was nice but as a couple we can't sitting,hanging hands together or a doing a funny things.. because one of the security lady coming and scolding us "don't doing this and this,this is a children's park" so after this stuff we are went out the park. I really hate this place and I'm not recommended this place to anyone.
title: This is a children's park can't walk freely as a couple

body: As a keen horticulturalist we took a walk through the park and met the head gardener . Never caught his name , but a great guy with a passion for plants. We spent an hour together walking around sharing our knowledge , and he gave us a personal tour of the parks special plants .Great that you can go half way around the world and meet someone with a very similar passion and interest.
title: Fantastic experience

body: I was deeply shocked to be asked for 300 rupees to enter this park. Whether this is the official foreigner rate or a scam I don't know. In England parks are free. I have no objection, as an overseas visitor, to making a reasonable contribution to Sri Lankan parks such as this but excessive demands will result in NO revenue. I just walked away.If an individual was trying to make a dishonest charge, he should be sacked. If not the authorities need to review their charges. It would be sensible if charges were advertised at the entrance. A tax rate of 0% or 100% will yield nothing. An excessive park charge will yield nothing.I love Sri Lanka and especially the people but beware of greed. Foreigners are not silly and news of bad experiences travels fast.
title: Beware entry fee rip-off

body: It is the onle place which will be guarnteed to hold a spot a soft place in our hearts! The romantic walks before tying the knot and later the visit with a kid and then with two! A place to make memories forever. Has an adequately well maintained Children park with makeshift (and safe) ferry's wheel, a small motored train with its own track and passenger carriages - Adults too can use it!! ;)
title: A family Treasure

body: the location is perfect in the down town.it's very well planned landscape and beautiful.whithin 1 hour can do that
title: in the city center

body: Nice Park, we'll maintained, good trees and greenery nice place to CHILL and relax good place to take pics
title: Nice park

body: not a bigger park like royal botanical garden or hakgala park but still an eco friendly, urban park. its like a park in England.
title: Little piece of heaven

body: The park is good for a family visit and children can play in the play area. It's a bit crowded, but still you can enjoy a relaxed walk or sit and enjoy the surrounding.
title: Good for a family visit

body: Good to see well maintained. Nice flowers and trees. A bit small but there is an old small bridge where can catch good picture.
title: Small but nice

body: A beautiful garden in Nuwara Eliya. There is a small entry fee. Good for a nice evening stroll. The flowers are beautiful though they are also seen in other parts of the Indian subcontinent. A few beautioful birds and monkeys also can be seen.
title: A NICE EVENING STROLL

body: This is a really beautiful park and has many attractive species of flora however it is badly maintained. The visitors seem to be thrashing the place too much which is a really sad site to see and simply ruins the whole landscape.
title: Badly Maintained but Beautiful Nonetheless

body: This place has a wide variety of plants.Has beautiful scenery.We enjoyed our visit thoroughly.A must visit if you are in Nuwara Eliya.
title: Beautiful

body: The call it botanical garden but actually it's not a real botanical, you'll find some kind of plants there but not endemic ones,anyway a calm and beautiful park for morning or afternoon walk.
title: Calm place in the city center

body: Really a nice place with nice climate and wonderful flowers, we all enjoyed with different plants and flowers. The garbage segregation bins were amazing...
title: Roses of heaven

body: Nice park- as non Sri Lankan you pay 300 rupees to get in. It's not as big as we thought and you could do this park in 15-30 mins. Lovely flowers. Some stray dogs around but not an issue.
title: Nice park

body: Victoria park is garden with full of flowers. Very close to Nuwara-Eliya city area. Able ti cover within 1hr.
title: Well managed

body: Very well taken care of and nice for a short stroll in the sun....you might get lucky and bump into one of the gardeners who will happily tell you more about the flowers, even in other languages!
title: Beautiful

body: The park was well maitained with a lot of people working for the great tourist season,which would start for the weekend,saturday 1/4.We went there for a couple of hours and realised that many of the flowers are common potted plants in Sweden.
title: A nice park among many others!

body: There are a different varieties of flowers and plants. There is a playground for children. Nice place to sit and read and relax.
title: Beautiful garden

One of the staff insisted on escorting her to an unmarked European wash room elsewhere in the park ,which he checked out before he let her use it.
title: A pleasant walk

body: Visited this park just before a rainy shower - beautiful variety of shrubs, flowers and trees, well maintained and thoughtfully designed. Heavy rainfall led to us taking shelter in the park's central shelter where we found many families enjoying their day out; we ended up making lots of new friends, young and old. There is a reasonably priced restaurant at the entrance with an adequate, if very limited menu, as well as a cafe inside the park serving drinks and snacks. Staff are friendly and helpful and the park was a welcome change from the frantic pace of the surrounding area. Stray dogs abound but pose no problem as they peacefully coexist with park goers and simply sit watching the world go by - I recommend you do the same in this beautiful park.
title: Interact with the locals

body: This park is situated right in the middle of the town. We were spending a little time here it was a nice place to walk around. This can be crowded on weekends and holidays. If you want to have a quick look of flowers this si a better place. If you with your partner it is a nice place to roam around.
title: Small in the middle of the town

body: Any place should be evaluated based on what it offers, not for what we hope to find there. Victoria Park was not meant to be a tourist attraction. It's a local public park with some interesting history.We visited in February and it seemed some of the beauty had faded away in the winter months and some planting and gardening works were going on. I bet it looks much more beautiful in Spring and Summer. We still found it to be a lovely park for a pleasant stroll while also exploring some of its historic areas and trees. The playground had lots of fun rides and our daughter enjoyed them a lot. Like most places we visited in Sri Lanka, mornings and evenings seem to be the best times to visit the park.Ticket prices are very reasonable and should be appreciated because the money goes into the maintenance and upkeep of the park. I recommend it for tourists who appreciate leisurely walks in relaxing settings.
title: A pleasant stroll

body: This is not terribly exciting but a pleasant place to spend an hour or 2. Several interesting birds and one of the gardeners took us under his wing, so to speak and showed us birds we would not have seen by ourselves.

body: The road from Kandy to Nuwara is a must see in Sri Lanka. The nature is remarkable. Then you get in Nuwara and oops, well, this is not Sri Lanka. The park itself is not something you cannot miss (it just look like a park) but the whole Nuwara is something different to feel in Sri Lanka.
title: Not the real Sri Lanka but still part of history

body: We visited the park with our two children, aged 9 & 10. You have to buy tickets to enter the park. There seems to be a scam going at the ticket office, where the posted price does not match the ticket price. The price for foreign adults is R300 each, but the children's admission price is not indicated. We gave R1200 and got four tickets and no change. Off we went to visit the park, however a short while later, on examining the tickets, we noticed that the children are charged at half price, i.e. R150! We went back to the ticket office to inquire and immediately the R300 change appeared, as if by magic...As for the park, it's quite pleasant but definitely overrated.
title: Nice park, but beware ticket scam if entering with children.

body: 300Rs for tourists, 40Rs for locals. I don't mind paying more, because I understand my money is worth more in Sri Lanka. However, I want to feel like I'm at least getting some value for my entrance fee, rather than just being taxed for being foreign. Some parts of the park were well maintained, but the rest is peppered with rubbish. The lily ponds have plastic bags floating in them. Some families had left the remains of their picnic spread all over the grass. There were food wrappers all along the paths and in the flower beds. The stream running through the park (the Nanu Oya) was full of rotting food wrappers and plastic bottles, needless to say we didn't see anything living in these waterways.And the saddest thing is that there are litter bins provided in many points in the park.I'm not sure exactly where all of the money from domestic and foreign tourists is going, so don't waste your time visiting, just have a look through the fence and you'll have a pretty good idea of what it's about.

body: The city is a base for visits to Horton Plains National Park. This is a key wildlife area of open grassy woodland. Species found here include the leopard, sambar, and the endemic purple-faced langur. Endemic highland birds include the dull-blue flycatcher, Sri Lanka white-eye, and yellow-eared bulbul. The plains have a well-visited tourist attraction at World's End — a sheer precipice with a 1050 m drop. The return walk passes the scenic Baker's Falls. Early morning visits are best, both to see the wildlife and to view World's End before mists close in during the later part of the morning.One of the distinctive features of Nuwara Eliya's countryside is the widespread growing of vegetables, fruit and flowers usually associated with temperate Europe. This "Little England" is covered with terraces growing potatoes, carrots, leeks, and roses, interspersed with tea bushes on the steeper slopes.The slow-growing tea bushes of this highland region produce some of the world's finest orange pekoe tea. Several tea factories around Nuwara Eliya offer guided tours and the opportunity to sample or purchase their products.
